scope: Active stream revocation through the real LUKS controller, host owner, session VM, gateway supervisor and broker; Mac ARM/HVF, nested TCG, synthetic SOCKS/TLS provider inside gateway VM.
network: Outer Debian VM has no NIC. Tor is offline; a lab-only SOCKS/TLS service runs on gateway loopback. No real provider request, API key, or packet capture in this run.

boundaries.storage: Real general and per-session LUKS2 volumes, one open session, normal controller close interlocks.
boundaries.controller_close: An active stream exists before close. Revoke closes its exact TLS connection and CLI reports error while session QEMU and LUKS mapping still exist; force-leave closes them afterward.
boundaries.qemu_exit: SIGKILL during a second stream is followed by grant/pidfd removal and closure of its TLS connection. Another session remains forbidden until explicit storage closure.
boundaries.trust_overlay: Only the laboratory Docker stage inserts one additional root certificate into the broker build. Exact diff retained. Repository broker source and production build retain fixed origin and public CA trust.
boundaries.diagnostics: Gateway private serial is enabled only in host lab-emulation build; production gateway keeps serial null. Status contains progressive stream IDs, errors and binary/fixture hashes, never payloads or credentials.
boundaries.synthetic_material: Committed certificate/private key are public fixture materials, used only by stream-* image stages.

session_cli.note: The raw runner summary opencode_sha256 describes the old base host image. This is the CLI actually installed in the new manifest-verified session image.
